patch_description: Use a continuation strategy rather than trusting one SLSQP pass from each grid perturbation.  Variable-radius packings have many nearly degenerate contact graphs: after the first joint center/radius solve, resolving the exact fixed-center LP exposes the preferred allocation of radius among contacts.  Restarting SLSQP from those improved centers with a larger iteration budget can release contacts that were prematurely frozen in the first solve.  The original seed and first-pass center arrangement are retained as candidates, so an unsuccessful nonlinear pass cannot discard a stronger LP arrangement.  A few extra asymmetric starts explore the important larger perturbation regimes while remaining far below the timeout.
